subject: Banking
title: Savings and Loan Disaster
description: Learn Savings and Loan Disaster in one minute.

hook.text: 1,043 savings and loan banks failed between 1986 and 1995. The government bailout cost taxpayers $132 billion.

buildup.text: S&Ls were community banks that took savings and made home loans.

discovery.text: With deposits insured by the government, S&L owners gambled freely. If they won, they kept profits.

twist.text: Charles Keating bribed five US senators to delay his S&L's investigation.

climax.text: The S&L crisis proved that deposit insurance without regulation creates moral hazard.

quiz.question: How many S&L institutions failed during the crisis?

details.summary: Over 1,000 savings and loan institutions failed in the 1980s and early 1990s after deregulation allowed them to make risky investments with government-insured deposits. The cleanup cost taxpayers $132 billion.
details.whyItMatters: The S&L crisis was the largest American financial disaster before 2008, proving that deregulation combined with government deposit insurance creates a moral hazard recipe for catastrophic losses.
takeaways: Over 1,000 S&L institutions failed between 1986 and 1995
Deregulation in 1982 allowed S&Ls to invest in risky commercial real estate
The Resolution Trust Corporation liquidated $394 billion in failed S&L assets

faq.question: What caused the savings and loan crisis?
faq.answer: S&Ls were deregulated to invest in commercial real estate and other high-risk assets while still backed by government deposit insurance. When real estate markets crashed, losses consumed the entire industry's capital and the insurance fund.

faq.question: How was the S&L crisis ultimately resolved?
faq.answer: Congress created the Resolution Trust Corporation to take over and sell failed S&L assets. The cleanup took years and cost taxpayers $132 billion. Stricter regulations prevented a repeat, though similar dynamics appeared in the 2008 crisis.
